sections.heading: EPDM Roofing Systems for East Orange Homes: Benefits and Downsides of EPDM Rubber

runs.v: is durable in an Essex County winter: it resists water, hail, snow, freeze-thaw cycles, heavy rain, UV exposure, ozone, and extreme temperature swings, and remains highly flexible in temperatures as low as -40°F. It is cost-effective compared to other low-slope roofing materials, easier to maintain than older flat systems, easily patched using specialized tape or adhesive, and its rubber surface discourages algae and moss growth. Black EPDM absorbs solar heat, which enhances winter heating efficiency and can reduce home heating costs.

The downsides of EPDM rubber roofing: seams that separate with age, punctures, edge shrinkage, summer cooling loads from standard black EPDM absorbing substantial solar heat, and an industrial look some homeowners find unappealing. A white membrane or reflective coating can improve energy efficiency under a top-floor bedroom.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for an EPDM roof on my East Orange building?

runs.v: An EPDM repair or replacement of the roof covering on a detached one- or two-family home counts as ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and requires no construction permit. On a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, repairing more than 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period requires a permit, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code. Permits go through the East Orange Building Division at City Hall, 44 City Hall Plaza.

faqs.q: How long does an EPDM rubber roof last on an East Orange apartment building?

runs.v: An EPDM rubber roof lasts 15 to 25 years, per InterNACHI; after 15 years, seams and flashing usually fail before the membrane field, so Newark Quality Roofing reseals those first.

faqs.q: Is EPDM or TPO flat roofing better for my East Orange rental property?

runs.v: Both are single-ply membranes: EPDM (15 to 25 years) fails most often at glued seams, TPO (7 to 20 years) at welded seams. Newark Quality Roofing matches the membrane to the building, its slope, and its access before any work begins.

faqs.q: Can EPDM be installed over the existing flat roof on my East Orange walk-up?

runs.v: Only when the existing assembly is dry and sound: the NJ Rehabilitation Subcode, N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4, requires removal of a water-soaked covering or one that already carries 2 or more layers, and a new layer over wet insulation traps the moisture. Many pre-war East Orange walk-ups carry patch-over-patch layers, so a full tear-off is often the right call.

faqs.q: Does an EPDM roof on an East Orange historic building need special approval?

runs.v: East Orange has no identified local historic-preservation ordinance, so a Certificate of Appropriateness is not triggered, and National Register listing alone places no restriction on a privately funded reroof, per the National Park Service. Verify current requirements with the East Orange Department of Planning, Policy & Development.
